utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you ready to start?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes. Good morning, Your Honour. I do believe Mr. Stojanovic has one more question, and I don't have any problem, as I indicated to him, if he asks it before I begin my cross-examination, subject, of course, to Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Yesterday after we reviewed the statement from the yesterday's cross-examination, we just needed another explanation, which I will require in the form of one question only. Thank you for your understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Stojanovic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, but if you could please just help us. Yesterday at one point you said that battalion commanders are under the command of the unit attached to this unit, exceptionally there is a possibility, in absence of the commander or chief of staff or other operations officers, higher-ranking officers, a duty operations officer could convey certain orders to you. Can you tell us under which regulation did you come to that conclusion.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's an internal regulation which is normally called the instruction for work of the duty operations officer. It prescribes that under all these extraordinary circumstances, when the duty operations officer has no one to consult with he can make a decision on his own. In other words, after he has exhausted all other possibilities, someone has to make a decision.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This instruction is an internal document adopted by the brigade commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you to the Chamber. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Cross-examined by Ms. Issa:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to start off with the -- one of the last documents that I believe was used in your examination-in-chief, the document signed by Ognjenovic, the previous commander of the Bratunac Brigade. Another officer testified that the statement to make life miserable for the Muslims in Srebrenica was actually made in order to boost the morale of the troops. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware, sir, that thousands of Muslims were murdered by the VRS army after the fall of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have learned about that from the press and from what is going on here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you didn't -- you're telling us that you weren't aware of it at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Objection. Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's not what he's saying, Your Honour. We're beginning the same process over and over again with this particular Prosecutor. Please look at the question, please look at his answer and then draw the conclusion from the following question. That's not what the gentleman said and the Prosecutor is being totally unfair on this point. And I mean totally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, we see no problem for the Prosecutor to ask this question. It's very logical.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, in my Aristotelian logic, it doesn't follow from that line of questioning. She can ask the question, but to say it's so based on the previous answer, it doesn't follow; not that logic. She's drawing some conclusions and I think she's being unfair with the witness. She can do aggressive cross-examination, I have no problem; but I want fair cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think it's a problem of the form of the question, actually and certainly there's no difference. Ms. Issa, you may put your question in the form of a question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you telling us then, sir, that you were not aware of the thousands of Muslims that were killed after the fall of Srebrenica during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when did you become aware of this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the topic reached the media, the press, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was after the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware, sir, that on the 25th of May, which was the first day that Colonel Blagojevic became commander of the brigade, that Srebrenica was shelled and a civilian was killed as a result of that shelling?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember that at all, and I don't know anything about that. And I don't see any reason why particularly on that day it should have been. On the day of the handover, I don't know what the purpose of that would be. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you believe, sir, that the thousands of Muslims were killed by the VRS army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't exclude that possibility, but it is up to you to demonstrate and prove whether that's the case or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking you whether or not you actually believed it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fact is that these people don't exist anymore. I don't know how many exactly, whether it's thousands. Probably it's a huge figure, but I can't say exactly. I didn't summarise these data. It is certain this is appalling what had happened, and I condemn this, but I didn't research this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But the question was whether you actually believed that the VRS army committed these crimes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at the time that you were asked this question, sir, in the interview in Banja Luka did you tell investigators whether or not you believed that it was the VRS army that committed these crimes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even now I don't want to say the VRS. It's too broad a notion. Maybe it was done by individuals or elements, but I can't say that the whole army was focused on that. I myself was a member of that army and I can guarantee for what I did at the time. As for the others, I can't say. In 1999, we can analyse what I said at that time as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, yesterday, sir, you were asked some questions by Mr. Stojanovic about the role of the duty officer. And you testified that the duty officer conveys information to the command from the battalions. Do you remember telling us that yesterday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it also true, sir, that the commander also conveys information to the battalions through the duty officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also testified, sir, that the battalions had engineering support. Wasn't the 5th Engineering Company at Lomenac Brook, where you were located, in order to mine that location between 6 July and 12 July, or during that period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 5th Engineering Company, it wasn't that. I had the 5th Infantry Company, not the Engineering Company, and they are not trained to do things like that. And even nowadays some civilian organisations are working on demining this area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's go to the I believe Exhibit P403, the minutes of the meetings of the command. We can go to that, please, with the assistance of Madam Usher. And in the English translation, we would be turning to page 8. And it's dated the 3rd of July. It's the last page in that series. I'll just read it out loud, sir, and then I'll ask you about it. "The assistant chief of staff for operations and training, problem of gap in the Lomenac brook must be resolved urgently. If possible, the engineering battalion from Konjevic Polje should be engaged to mine this location." Can you tell us what the problem was there, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The problem was that according to some earlier information that we had had or intelligence that we received, enemy groups infiltrated across this creek, their sabotage and reconnaissance group. And for the purpose of closing this gap which was not a very big one, but nevertheless there was a gap, I requested that it be -- engineering works be done there because this is a very delicate area in terms that it leads towards the town and the road. And that was a problematic area itself if it were to become accessible for passage. Even before that there were minefields in that area and unfortunately they still do exist there. And I know that some civilian organisations are demining it. That's it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to another area. Now, yesterday, sir, you were asked a number of questions, and I believe as well on Tuesday in your examination-in-chief, regarding the term "zone of responsibility." Were you aware, sir, that the map you were shown yesterday that was entitled the "zone of responsibility," "Bratunac Brigade zone of responsibility" was in fact seized from the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose that was the case, that it was seized.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Were you aware of that or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. This particular map, it doesn't mean anything in particular to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, yesterday, sir, you said - I believe it was at page 22, line 18 of your transcript - that "a battalion does not have a zone of responsibility, not even a brigade has one." Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in your examination-in-chief on Tuesday, you said: "According to the rules that were in force and that were in force and that we observed, a battalion has its own area of defence, not a zone of responsibility." And you also said: "I don't even know this term 'zone of responsibility.'". Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The term itself was used, but I can't give an expert opinion or find any for that, nor can I find where it is based in the military theory or practice. It was a jargon term that kind of its way into everyday usage but I don't know where it came from. If you can tell me where this term can be found, certifying that either a battalion or a brigade had zones of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, I'm simply quoting from your statement or your evidence on Tuesday. Now, yesterday you told us that this term was used. On Tuesday you told us: "I don't even know this term zone of responsibility."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's been asked and it's been answered. And I believe he posed a question. Now, whether the Prosecutor can demonstrate where in the rules, for the brigade or battalion, there's a zone of responsibility she can produce it. But I believe he did give an explanation, so it's an asked and answered. And I would also ask the Prosecutor to point exactly where the rules say for brigade or battalion that they have a zone of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Karnavas is interfering with my cross-examination. I don't have to conduct it in the way that he's suggesting. And I'm simply asking a follow-up question, which I believe I'm entitled to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I believe. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, sir, on Tuesday you told us: "I don't even know this term 'zone of responsibility.'" And yesterday you told us it was used informally. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe I wasn't clear enough. I -- in the military theory and practice, I am not able to give you an expert explanation. I can't find it anywhere. If you can do so, please be my guest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's go to your transcript from yesterday's testimony. And I'm reading from page 39 at about line 3. And you say, again yesterday: "I wouldn't be able to say who could draw a zone of responsibility, which as I emphasised did not exist at a term. So I have no idea who could possibly have made this map." So therefore again, sir, you say that this term does not exist.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how many times I have to repeat this in order to make myself sufficiently clear. At the level of a brigade or a battalion, in the military theory and practice it doesn't exist. It is a fact that it's written in the report, but who wrote it, whether it was a professional and/or a trained officer has written this, I doubt that one would do that. Maybe it was done by an amateur.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Is that a term that you would use, sir? Or maybe it was done by an amateur.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I shouldn't use it either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's go to the interview in Banja Luka. I'm going to give you a copy of your transcript with the assistance of Madam Usher. Thank you very much. In the English version if you could turn to page 24, line 12. And for you, sir, in the B/C/S version page 26, starting at line 15, and then moving down on to page 27. I'm just going to start reading your answer. You say: "It was for -- which belonged to the Muslim" -- there's something unintelligible there. "And it was of interest to me to observe the positions which the Bosniaks sat there on that line, to confirm what I have previously conceived about their way of contacting defence, and I was going around their position to see how they had established their defence and all of what they said is true. That all what I have said is true, I offer you the possibility of checking my story with any of my soldiers by method of casual sample. I won't suggest anyone. You can pick anyone you want. I don't mind if you want to ask where we were on that day." And then you go on and you say: "Under the condition, of course, that they were not somewhere outside the zone of responsibility. Some were ill." And it goes on. So in your interview, sir, you used that term yourself. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if it was correctly translated. Because you have emphasised and mentioned so many times zone of responsibility, it maybe entered my vocabulary as well. But I stand by my assertion that in theory, in professional theory of military practice, the theory doesn't exist. I said that it was an amateurish and jargon term.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let's go to page 23, line 13. And I believe for you, sir, it's at page 22, 21. And you're being asked. Question: "Okay. Kravica would be on this map here. Okay. So in this area here -- so this would not be your area of responsibility?" And you answer: "My zone of responsibility ended at Ilina Bara, this 555."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't find it here. If someone would help me, please. But when I explained what the defence sector was, would you please also include that. Don't skip that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, I'm simply referring to the actual term at the time being. That's just another example of you using the term in your interview.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: But please don't overlook the fact that I'm referred to the defence sector and the depth of defence at the time as well. I think that Mr. Harmon and Mr. Ruez, who questioned me at the time, insisted on that term. And it may have been that I also used this incorrect term. But could you please find the part in my statement where I explained what the defence sector was and what the -- in depth of the defence sector implied.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, the question has nothing to do with the defence sector. The question was simply whether or not you used that term, and I think you explained yourself now. Let's go to a different area. Thank you very much, Madam Usher. I don't think I will be needing the assistance of the transcript for the time being. Now, sir, you were asked questions about daily combat reports in your examination-in-chief, and you discussed each -- well, many of them. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, all of these reports - and we could look at them - actually go out under the name of the commander. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he would be responsible for their contents. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In indirect manner, yes. But these reports were written on his behalf by duty operations officer or other responsible officer present on the spot. That's the practice even nowadays, commander signs reports but the reports are compiled either by an operations organ or a duty operations officer. The commander doesn't always have the time to look into it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're saying he signed the reports without reading them?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Objection. That's not what he said and that's -- she's not pointing at any signed reports by Colonel Blagojevic at the time. If you could kindly listen to the answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: There's a distinction between a report being made between an operations officer and sent to the Drina Corps when the commander is not there versus the one the commander prepares and signs himself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I think you raised your objection. That's enough. Yes, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I think the witness answered the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Wouldn't it be normal, sir, for the battalion and specifically the battalion commander to provide daily combat reports to the brigade command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be understandable if it were feasible, but I don't know in which form are you referring to, depending on what the battalion has at its disposal in terms of communications devices. If it is possible to send a telegram, just as was the case with the brigade command, then it's feasible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, just like the brigade provides daily combat reports to the Drina Corps and the Drina Corps provides reports to the Main Staff and so on and so forth, isn't it normal for the people on the ground, the battalions, to provide the information to the brigade by way of reports?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the way it should be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So any information regarding things such as captured prisoners or the location of the enemy, et cetera, in the brigade daily combat reports would, in fact, be coming from the battalion reports, wouldn't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not understand that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Any information regarding a specific battalion, sir, that is noted by the duty officer would be coming from -- in the brigade daily combat reports would be coming from the battalion, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily only from the battalion. There could be many other sources of information apart from those reports. The commander himself can find himself in the field and observe things that are essential and important. There are many items that are reported on. It can happen that somebody else from various organs of the command makes his own contribution to the report. It's not necessarily that the battalion is the only source of information. There can be others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, information regarding a particular battalion where a particular battalion is located and information relating to the enemy or captured prisoner, wouldn't that come from the battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only from the battalion. Others, too, can observe the enemy and everything else, even civilians can. Some organ or authority from that territory can be a source of information. There are many ways in which information can be obtained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you're also telling us though, sir, that the battalion can also be a source of information, can it not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, what happened to the daily reports that your battalion provided?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: First I have to emphasise that during those days we had rather poor communications with our superior command for a variety of reasons. First of all, I spent almost all my time at my forward command post, from which I had no wire communications, that is to say secure communications that couldn't be jammed or listened to. And second, we had very great problems with our means of communications with our equipment. And they were very old, in poor working order, batteries were often low or empty. We had a problem charging them, and we were often without any means of communication. So there was an exchange of information, but not in a very large scope.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But the question was, sir: What happened to the reports that you provided to the brigade? Where are they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, you testified yesterday that you were part of a commission in 1997 where documents were handed over to you from the brigade. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps, sir, for --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Actually, Your Honour, perhaps we can go into private session very briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If I can get the assistance of Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, on Tuesday you testified that you had no artillery during that period --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And yesterday after we looked at the -- and I believe it's in your examination-in-chief looking at the July 5th minutes of the brigade command meeting --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were asked if you can explain the purpose of "increasing the accuracy and direction of artillery fire." And that was in relation to the chief of staff coming down to your battalion to increase the accuracy and direction of artillery fire. Do you remember being asked about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. It's a bit complicated. If I was talking about the firing system, that's something I can explain. More specifically, that's something that the chief of artillery should have adjusted. But I'm not really quite clear. What exactly are you asking?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, in the July 5th minutes of the meeting that we saw yesterday it says: "The chief of staff will go to the 1st Battalion to increase accuracy and direction of the artillery fire." And you were asked if that occurred and you said it has. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on Tuesday, sir, you also told us that you had mortars.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And yesterday - and I'm referring to page 47, line 3 - I believe you said you didn't. So which is it? Did you have mortars or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, mortars do not count as artillery. Yesterday, in one brief answer I emphasised there were in the structure in infantry units. Those people who operate them do not have the military economic specialty of artillery men. They are trained to operate them as infantrymen. I said that I did not have mortars, and that's clear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. On Tuesday, sir, you said you did have mortars. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you even now that I had mortars. We did have mortars. I'm not denying at any point that we had mortars. I'm just saying that a mortar is not considered as an artillery piece in our army. And maybe in some other armies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I appreciate that, sir, and I'm not asking you about artillery pieces at the time. Right now I'm just asking you about mortars. And yesterday I'm going to quote you from your transcript.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Page 49, line 16, you say: "I did not have combat support. I have this line, only the first line of defence. All this behind within the framework of companies I did not have. I didn't have mortars, nor did I have any anti-armour weapons within companies, nor did I have the second-echelon company, or the light artillery rocket platoon. So many of the things from this general scheme are lacking in my structure in those days." So the question, sir, is you either had mortars or you didn't. Now, are you telling us now you had mortars?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember what I said on that occasion. I said I did not have mortars within the framework of companies. Maybe that was misinterpreted. When I was looking at that diagram, within the composition of that diagram it says: "Company firing group." Those are mortars; that I didn't have. And at battalion level, I had them; every battalion had them. Now, if you go into it what kind of mortar and in what condition they were, that's another matter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you fire from your position at all at anybody during the period of 6 to 12 July, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not against observed targets, but in a preventive manner. When I was entering the area of Cizmici, I fired against trig point 413 and on some former trenches where the enemy used to be, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you fire at the UN observation post located in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not mad. Why would I do that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware, sir, of the DutchBat observation post November, located right in front of your position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was obvious.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was obvious, so you saw it there. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to the UN report, sir, on Friday, 7 July, this observation post was shelled by mortar fire. One shell struck the entrance of the observation post, and one the protective wall. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, and I believe that is really not true. On the 7th of July, that we were firing?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was the question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm saying it's untrue. It's untrue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. What about on the 8th of July? According to the --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Not then either. I am telling you with absolute certainty that I did not shoot at the post, absolutely not. You can perhaps check, even now, even today, whether there are any remains of shells, but I tell you for a fact I did not shoot at the observation point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, according to the report, sir, on 8th of July it says: "The intensity of the shelling increased that day. 15 mortar shells struck at a short distance from the observation post." And then on Sunday 9 July it was quiet until the 12th of July. And then on the 12th of July at approximately 2.30, it says: "The observation post was shelled by artillery and mortars for ten minutes. The shots fell just next to the observation post. Three anti-tank missiles then struck the observation post. Immediately afterwards, a group of Bosnian Serb army soldiers ran up the hill firing their weapons. In the end, there were some 60 Bosnian Serb army soldiers in the observation post. DutchBat personnel were disarmed and the vehicle was plundered. At the end of the afternoon they arrived in Bratunac under Bosnian Serb army escort." Are you telling us, sir, that all of that didn't happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The way it sounds in this report, it's like a scenario for a film. I have to tell you that this observation point, first of all, was located in front of my positions as much as it was in front of the positions of other battalions. It was like in the palm of your hand. If I had wanted to do something, I could have targeted it and shot it from my self-propelled gun at any moment. However, I didn't give any orders to do any such thing; I did not have any such orders. I have the impression that it's somebody's screenplay. I really cannot understand it. It's totally inconceivable.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, this is a very serious matter and I wouldn't be referring to it as a screenplay. Did you actually observe the observation post being shelled?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you saw nothing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That point was not targeted; it wasn't targeted for sure. I emphasised that while we were entering into that area, trenches were in that territory and the observation point allowed enemy soldiers to fortify all the time. They were digging trenches before their very eyes. I could not stop to check whether the enemy was there at the time or not. In one of the official reports, it was noted that in front of the observation point, in front of the observation point at that time in that period, enemy soldiers in trenches were observed. So I could not allow it to happen that somebody from those trenches should kill my soldiers. That has absolutely nothing to do with the observation point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, the question was, sir: You did not see the observation post being shelled. And you've told us you haven't. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware, sir, that the Muslim men in the column that were going through the woods were ultimately -- many of whom were ultimately murdered?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Again, what does that have to do with the observation post that was shelled and incidentally there was no testimony by any Dutch soldiers or Karremans was never brought here by the Prosecution to tell us how he was personally attacked at that post. What does the post have to do with the column of the men?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe that's another subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It could be. It could be. But the way it's posed, it's fused, one would think that --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm objecting to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: It's totally inappropriate for Mr. Karnavas to keep standing up making his own comments, essentially attempting to testify. He does this every single time. We all see what he was doing. It's pretty obvious I was moving on to another subject. There was no fusing here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, the question was: Are you aware that the Muslim men in the column, many of whom were ultimately murdered?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only through newspaper reports when all these events were over. In 1996, I already started to read about it. But at that time that I should have been aware of it, that I had any knowledge, that I was an eyewitness, no, that is not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, maybe we can go to your map, the map that you marked on Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If I can have the assistance of Madam Usher. Thank you. P186/1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, just to confirm your location, sir, as I understood your testimony, your command post was located at Bozici. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Bozici, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please take the pointer and point that out for us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the 6th of July, we were around this area here, Bozici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you remained there until the 12th. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until the 12th, with the proviso that I spent most of my time at the forward command post. I would be there all day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say to us before the 6th of July you were in the area of Bozici, how long were you there before the 6th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, perhaps a year or two. Because our command post used to be at another location and we moved in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So for about a year or two you were located mostly -- largely at Bozici. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you testified, as I understand it, on the 12th of July you moved a little bit more forward down to Cizmici, if I'm pronouncing that correctly; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that arrow that you have pointing in the direction is where you say you saw the column moving, the column of men. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which arrow you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, there's an arrow, sir, that appears to be going in the direction on the left side of the map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is that the one?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I showed that there was a gap there between the Milici and the Bratunac Brigades. That's what it means. And this column took this direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So that's where the column was moving or what you saw?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, the Court has heard evidence that there were thousands of Muslim men flooding the area behind the lines and into Susnjari and Jaglici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Behind which lines? Whose lines?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Behind --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Behind or in front of? I don't understand your question. Behind the lines, in front of the lines? I'm totally at a loss here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It would be both behind and in front. They were flooding the area. You didn't see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct, that they flooded the area behind the lines and the rest of it. That's not true. The column was moving along one trodden road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they were all moving single file along just one road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the way we saw them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't see anyone moving into the Susnjari and Jaglici area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This column was moving towards Jaglici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You didn't receive any orders at all regarding the column, sir, the thousands of men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no particular orders other than that we monitor the situation and try to avoid any possible surprises.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if you wanted to, sir, you could have called the artillery unit and called in the coordinates of the column. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That column was not directly in front of me, it was more to my right-hand flank in front of the 4th Infantry Battalion, which you can see here. You can see where the battalion was and where Jaglici is. So directly in front of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the question was: If you had wanted to, you could have called in the coordinates of the column?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could maybe just give a more precise location, but I don't know about the coordinates. I could just tell what their direction -- what direction they were moving in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, witnesses from the column, sir, have reported that they have been shelled on the 12th and 13th of July. Did you know about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were fighting those days. Shots were heard coming from different directions, particularly in the area of Bokcin Potok. There was fighting constantly going on there. I can't be more specific than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see the column being shelled?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We heard detonations, so I can presume that was that. Let me tell you, first this particular location is a very inconvenient one to be targeted. It's the very peak and it's difficult for a gun, for instance, that our artillery had to engage this target because they cannot engage this in a so-called upper angle of firing. And we from the artillery know that it's very difficult to hit a peak, and that is what I could see from my sector.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the blue lines on the map that you drew that you marked on Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, that represented the order that you were given on 14 July to sweep the terrain. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a very rough term. A more proper term would be to search the terrain. To tell you frankly, I didn't -- I don't recall seeing this order. I tried to construe this order here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, that's the question, sir, that you -- what you marked on the map is what the order was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if we look at that line and we look at where you saw the column, that goes right into the column, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, according to this, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: But the order dated the 14th was given when -- at the time when the column was not there any longer. As I said, we moved on the 16th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you report back to Colonel Blagojevic that you didn't follow the order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already told you that I didn't see this specific form of the order. And as you could see at the top of this order, you can see that it's addressed to the chief of staff. And we did not act in that manner, but rather, where we found ourselves at the moment, we continued to move from there forward.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, you say you didn't see a specific form of the order. Did you or did you not receive the order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you did receive the order. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did receive it, but not in this form. And I really cannot remember the exact moment when we did receive it. I just assumed that we did receive it, but I cannot recall the time and the way in which it had been conveyed to us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, the question was then, sir: Did you report to Colonel Blagojevic, your commander, that the order was not followed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since I cannot recall the time specified for us to set off on the mission of the searching the terrain, I cannot remember. But I presume that the commander knew at the time where we were. But just as we didn't move, the 2nd Battalion didn't move as well. In addition, the chief of staff was there with me until the 12th, and he probably reported back to the commander how far we had reached on the 12th. So perhaps I thought it wasn't necessary for me to report back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, as I understood your testimony --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I think I'm finished with the map. Thank you very much Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As I understood your testimony, sir, on Tuesday you said that you didn't know about the attack on Srebrenica before 6th July. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware, sir, of the observation post, the DutchBat observation post, OP Echo, located at Zeleni Jadar in May and June of 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that somewhere in the area around Zeleni Jadar it was located, but I didn't know the specific site.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware, sir, of what happened to it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that it was shelled, forcing the DutchBat to abandon the observation post?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know anything specifically about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you send personnel to Zeleni Jadar before the attack on Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had about four or five men in the area of Zeleni Jadar, but all units assigned the so-called temporary manpower for that specific area. But I cannot say exactly whether they were in Zeleni Jadar or in Pribicevac or I can't even remember the names of the soldiers who were there at the time. I proposed once that this be manned by different soldiers. And I think that it was manned by members of the Workers' Battalion, but I cannot confirm the names of my soldier. If you have this kind of information, maybe we can try and see whether it is really true or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So now you're telling us you are unable to remember the names of your own soldiers who were sent to Zeleni Jadar?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Again, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I just want to object. You're telling us now as if he had told something previously. So again, these are very unfair. Just look at the question, Your Honour: You're telling now, as opposed to whether on a previous occasion he mentioned the names of those particular soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, well, I don't see any problems with this question. Maybe I'm not as concentrated as you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Maybe I didn't get enough sleep, Your Honour, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may proceed, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't recall the name, sir, of your own soldiers who were sent to Zeleni Jadar before the Srebrenica operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you be able to give me 500 names of the people you know? Could you remember the names of your classmates from your secondary school? This is totally irrelevant, the names of these people. I don't know who they are and why -- my memory is not so good. Maybe it's your -- respectfully, your memory is good, but I really can't remember all the names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, you told us it was four or five people, with all due respect, not 500. That's why I'm asking the question. You don't recall that, is what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: (redacted). Do you understand that? And these people were sent there by lower-ranking officers, for example, company commanders. Why should I know where each and every soldier is at every point in time? It was not my job to know that. I don't have a flying carpet to see and observe where and what every soldier was doing. I'm not a wizard. I really can't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I didn't ask you, sir, whether or not you were a wizard. The question was very simple. You could have answered it by saying yes or no, but I think I understand your answer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I think, Your Honour, it is the time for the break and I'm prepared to stop here at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll have a break and we'll resume at quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If I can just get the assistance of Madam Usher, I'd like to refer to the map once again that the witness marked. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, sir, could you take that pointer and point out where the observation post November was located in front of you, the DutchBat observation post in front of you when you were at Bozici.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. Approximately here in this part, there's a clearance here but I cannot say exactly. This is where the 2nd Battalion was and this is where my battalion was, both could have been seen from that observation point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So just -- if -- to be clear, it's just slightly north of Cizmici. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sort of, above Cizmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Sir, getting back to questions we were dealing with before the break, you told us that you sent about four or five men to Zeleni Jadar before the Srebrenica operation. I'd like to refer to P863/A.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: With the assistance of Madam Usher, we can just refer to that document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, that's dated 4 June 1995 from the Pribicevac forward command post, Bratunac Brigade to the Trisic command under the name of Colonel Blagojevic. And if you look at paragraph 1 - and I'll read it out slowly - "I hereby order: The commander of the 1st Infantry Battalion shall assign a platoon of 27 men (Platoon leader, 24 men to take up positions, 2 men from the logistics platoon for logistical support). The platoon shall occupy four trenches to the right of the asphalt road between the village of Zeleni Jadar and Srebrenica." So in fact, sir, there were 27 men that were sent, not four or five. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I said four or five men in July. This is June, the 4th of June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I think the question was before the operation of Srebrenica. I didn't ask -- tell you a specific month. Was there another set of men sent in July as well to the Zeleni Jadar area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I know of. How many people in total were there? I suppose there were four or five because there was one trench there. In the meantime, we were receiving reinforcements from the Workers' Battalion. Maybe my colleague, who was the commander of the 3rd Infantry Battalion, would know better about that, how many men there were and how deployed they are. However, in the meantime before the operation in Srebrenica started, about one month had elapsed. So in that meantime, many things could have been changed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So -- but according to this document, 27 men would have been sent to the Zeleni Jadar --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what is written here, but it's a different question whether they were actually dispatched. Quite often we had tremendous problems in deploying people to other areas, whether in any battalion, Pjenovac, or any other sector. It does not necessarily mean that there were exactly 27 men sent there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go to the next page, paragraph 9.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that says: "Keep the reconnaissance platoon of the 1st Infantry Battalion in the region of the village of Zeleni Jadar (UNPROFOR checkpoint between 5" -- sir, let me finish reading. "Between 5 June and 9 June 1995 (replacing the military police)), and after two days of rest, integrate into the original unit on 12 June at 0900 hours." Do you see that there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, were you aware that this area, Zeleni Jadar, was the axis of the attack on Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that the attack was launched along that axis, but not towards Srebrenica, but rather to cut the line or the route because connecting the two enclaves, those of Zepa and Srebrenica. That was the purpose.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: But not at that time. That was not an objective at that time. That was an objective on the 6th of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's move on to something else. Going back to the minutes of the meetings of the Bratunac Brigade, which is at P403. Page 8 in the English translation. Now, that says: "The battalion commanders have submitted analysis of combat readiness, and it will be completed by tomorrow." And then the second-to-last line --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And then the second-to-the-last line says: "Battalion commanders will stay with me and the chief of staff."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go to another exhibit, D179/1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Ms. Issa, I think I have to remind you that this witness is a protected witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you. Okay. Perhaps, Your Honour, we -- and I appreciate the reminder. Perhaps we can go into private session just for the next few questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you only heard about that from the media. When did you hear about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, around 1996 I heard about that. I heard some stories. I believe some footage was shown and something like that. But specifically I don't even remember from which particular mass medium I learnt about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, if we can go to the next exhibit. I just want to show you a map which I believe has already been admitted into evidence, which is P566.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can -- if I can ask that the Glogova area be blown up on the ELMO so we all can see it more clearly, where it says numbers 1 and 2 on the axis 96. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, your command post was in Bozici. Can you point to that, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. This part here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And we see that it says Bozici just below that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Above that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you see the numbers 1 and 2 on the map there, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you realise, sir, that those are the mass graves that were created within about a kilometre of your command post in Bozici?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now counsel is testifying about a kilometre. I take it she is going to testify to us that it was a kilometre from the command post to where these are located.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Ask a question to this witness. Ask this witness to tell you what's the distance.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Perhaps I can find another way, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Then I would ask that the question be noted as having no value whatsoever, because the witness -- the Prosecutor just indicated that it was a kilometre away. I take it she had a good-faith basis in making that assertion. If she has a good-faith basis, I would like to know what it was. If she is just guesstimating, I would like to know that she was just guesstimating based on the distance on this map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we are waiting for the questions from the Prosecution at this moment. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour. And just to clarify, the squares on the map are approximately a kilometre each. It's a map that I believe was made to scale.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We see there, sir, your command post at Bozici, which is very close to the graves. There's no question about that. The graves were located where they are located on the map. Do you realise that they were created that close to your command post?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, they are not as close as you seem to represent. Looking at the map I believe you have no military training, and that is why you said what you said, namely that it is 1 kilometre. This is actually much more than a kilometre, even as a crow flies. And on the ground it is even more. If you wish, we can do a professional terrain profile and see how much the distance exactly is. Can you tell me exactly how the -- when those graves were created as far as you know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They were created, sir, between the 13th of July and 14th of July.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well. I told you a moment ago where I was on the 12th and where my command post was -- or more precisely, where my former command post was. We are talking about my former command post. Is that all right?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So you don't know anything about that, right, is what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you moved everything, your command post that had been there for two years, the quartermasters, the equipment, everything, in one day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't move everything. The command post is not linked to the logistics. Those are two different things. I didn't move everything. Some elderly men and people who cooked food remained. It was not a very unwieldy unit. In fact, we had some women for cooking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So those people remained at the command post and - according to this map, which is to scale - within a kilometre where the graves were created. Right? Just answer the question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you kindly, since you claim it is a kilometre, prove it is a kilometre. I say that isn't. Second of all, I would be grateful if you would emphasise that it is my former command post, meaning that it did not exist as a command post.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's approximately 1 or 2 kilometres from your command post, sir --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. I mean, I really don't like interrupting, but the gentleman has indicated that he can demonstrate to us professionally how far it was. And so now it went from a kilometre, because the squares are a kilometre, to now 1 to 2. So if Ms. Issa knows exactly, she can tell us rather than just guessing because of the blocks. Otherwise, either accept the gentleman's answer or allow the gentleman to demonstrate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I don't think that is important, how far the distance is. But as a matter of fact, it's very near, very close --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If you look at the map itself, it might look close.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But we don't know what the terrain looks like, we don't know visibility, we don't know any of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The question is whether the witness knew about the graves or not. This is the gist of the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I believe he's answered that question, Your Honour, that he did not. But I'm willing to sit here and she can ask the question over again. I don't care.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I think we all get the point, so I just have maybe one or two more questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you testified in your examination-in-chief, sir, that you were at the meeting of 16 October 1995, where Nikolic stated: We are currently engaged in tasks issued by the Army of Republika Srpska, asanacija. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think the interpretation is correct, because it was emphasised that it was the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What it says, sir, is: "We are currently" - this is at the meeting that you were present at on October 16, 1995 - "engaged in tasks issued by the Army of Republika Srpska, General Staff, asanacija." I'm reading that, a quote.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I would like the record to quote that in the previous question General Staff was omitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wasn't quoting in the previous question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I didn't hear the General Staff appear, it only appeared in the answer of the witness. Maybe there's a problem of misunderstanding there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Or maybe there was an omission, a purposeful omission by the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe Ms. Issa could ask another question to this witness so that to clarify this issue for us.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I attempted to clarify to the witness because of the question he asked me, and I quoted directly. And I think that for Mr. Karnavas to continuously make these outrageous allegations is extremely inappropriate and disrespects the very process that we are engaged in. And it happens all the time, as we know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, notwithstanding that you were at the meeting and asanacija was talked about, you don't know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know what the term "asanacija" means, but do you know what it means? It doesn't have to mean anything that terrible. Asanacija or clearing of the terrain is a preventive action and a normal action that is undertaken after a battle. One of the reasons why it is done is to prevent contamination or infection by contagious diseases. And a number of other actions are implied. It is to be undertaken by logistical organs, organs in charge of moral and some other organs. It is not a very fortunate subject for a person to deal with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, I believe that the Prosecutor asked you a very simple question. In most of the cases, the question could be answered simply by saying yes or no. If you have some questions, you could ask for some clarification. So please concentrate on the question put to you by the Prosecutor. The question is very simple. Did you know anything about that? It's a yes or no question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Apart from having heard that term, I didn't know anything else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to clarify, sir, there was no battle at the time in October, was there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Are you aware, sir, that several soldiers or members of the Bratunac Brigade have testified that they were engaged in the reburial operation that occurred in October?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: They are military police officers, Your Honour. There's a distinction between being a soldier and a military police officer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, the witness could answer that question if he knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, if she was to pose it properly and accurately, that military police officers testified, I don't have a problem. But to say "soldiers" encompasses a wide and broad area and could be very misleading. If he says no, he appears to be dishonest.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I actually also stated members of the Bratunac Brigade. I don't think you can get more general than that and I think perhaps Mr. Karnavas should listen more carefully.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I just want to note the personal attacks constantly on me. I'm being accused of personally attacking the Prosecutor. I'm sitting here taking my medication from the Prosecutor. So I want the record to reflect that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, the question is: "There were soldiers or members of the Bratunac Brigade have testified. They were engaged in the reburial operation that occurred in October." There's no problem with this question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of that, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I have nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any re-direct examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have a few questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just some matters of clarification. Re-examined by Mr. Karnavas:

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we could have that map back again, I believe it was 566.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could assist us in answering some of the questions you were not able to answer before. Now, just for clarity's sake, knowing -- I take it you do know the terrain that we're speaking of, where your command post was and where we see numbers 1 and 2?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Knowing the terrain, could you please first tell us what is the terrain like. Is it flat ground? Is it mountainous? What's the visibility level from where you are to these locations?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's totally leading. He could simply have asked him: What is the terrain like? Without going through this multiple choice that he just went through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: If this is a direct examination, I would say that is leading. But this is re-direct. I think the leading question is allowed in this occasion. You may proceed, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just please describe to us what the terrain looked like.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This terrain was very difficult, inaccessible. This road which you see in behind here was overgrown. There were some trees there, and it simply wasn't used for communication for the simple reason that it was easier to use the asphalt road here than this one. There were some houses there, destroyed by previous action. There were also minefields laid during earlier battles that we assumed were there still. So this terrain was not used for supply routes or for any other sort of communication. And it is also hilly, as you can see on the map. It is wooded and hilly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Could you please tell us to your understanding and knowledge of the terrain what's the distance that we're talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we look at the distance by walking on the road, it could be 3 and a half to 4 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about if we just look -- can you look from your command post to those locations and observe them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because there are natural obstacles such as woods. It's simply impossible. There's no way you can see anything. And it is also shielded. If my command post was here and there is a curve between my command post and this location, so you cannot see it anywhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you please tell us where you had moved the location. You showed us where you were on the -- up until the 12th, and then you indicated that you had moved. And if we were to accept the Prosecution at their word, that these occurred on the 13th and 14th, these graves, please tell us where you would have been at that point in time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this area here, Cizmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where again? Could you please show us that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This area, Cizmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, from that area, could you please tell us what the distance is from Cizmici to 1 and 2.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As the crow flies it's at least 4 kilometres or thereabouts. And the terrain is terribly difficult to cross. There are no communications. There were many minefields in that area and it is along this route that some of my soldiers got killed, including that commander I told you about. It's an extremely inaccessible, impassable route, terrain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us from that location what the visibility would have been like. Can you get a clear view from Cizmici to where, say, you see 1 and 2?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The visibility is nil. You could not observe anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, could you please tell us why.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same reason, natural obstacles, woods. It was in a depression, shielded by some elevations, therefore you could not observe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you please just describe -- show us a little bit from where you were located on the 12th, in which direction and how you moved your troops to Cizmici. Did you -- in other words, did you go by 1 and 2 or did you go by another direction? Which way did you go?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe it was already asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, he asked the witness to show on the map what's the road from the former command post to the new one. I think it is necessary for the Court to understand that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I moved from these areas -- from this area here of Vresinje, using these routes here, from Pajici to Cizmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about from the command post, where you were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Where was the command post on the 12th? Show us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, that's where you -- well, was that established on the 12th or was it there before the 12th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't there before the 12th. We established this command post on the afternoon of the 12th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I can clear it up, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I don't know if that's where Mr. Karnavas is going. I was just trying to assist, Your Honour. I think he was referring to the forward command post, just to make sure that the record isn't unclear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I think that. I think the following question will ask the witness to identify the former command post. And we just want to know the road he travelled to the new command post. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I may direct your attention so that Mr. McCloskey doesn't whisper too much to his colleague about me clearing this up --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, this is unnecessary --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It is, but it's very interrupting. It's extremely interrupting and I'm trying to do re-direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's the third attack on us today, Your Honour. I'm sorry to interrupt. There's a difference between the forward command post, the former command post, and the command post. It's a little bit confusing. I know it's late in the day and we're trying to help on that particular issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's all we're trying to do. Most of my whispering is designed to communicate with my counsel. That may not be how this man works. But to do this in the middle of the testimony repeatedly like this it's really -- it's appalling.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I don't need any help from the Prosecution. When the time comes, if it ever, God help me, I might ask. But at this point in time, I don't need any help.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, put your question to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, earlier when you were being questioned by the Prosecutor, you told us, before you moved your troops, where the command post was located. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please point that out to us. We're talking before you moved.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now we want to know which direction you moved toward when you established your new post, because you indicated you moved on the 12th and 13th.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
