utterances.text: I would like to avoid any confusion here, because as I understood the Prosecution, they believe that a forward command post was in Cizmici. It was a command post there. The forward command post was formerly in Vresinje, which we don't see here in the map. That is where the forward command post used to be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, having clarified that, could you please tell us, show us, the direction when you moved from one location to the next.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I came here from the Vresinje sector, after these units entered from these directions. And then I joined them from the Vresinje sector where my forward command post was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, one last question on this map. When you and your troops moved, did you or any of your troops go by the area where 1 and 2 is designated on the map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there was no need. What kind of role was that to be played? No way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just want the record to be clear on that. Okay, thank you. We can move on. I don't need the map anymore. Thank you. Now, I just want to start from the beginning, hit a couple of points. You were asked about reports, you as the -- what sort of reports would have been submitted. Now, in watching the occupying forces in Iraq, we see soldiers with computers, laptops, wiring into a foreign country where they have an operations war room going on. Could you please tell us: How many computers did you have available at the terrain so you could wire in e-mail, send in your reports in a written fashion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't have any modern equipment. Maybe I would just like to draw your attention to something that should be borne in mind, and that is military task and obligation to monitor the situation on the ground. And this process differs largely, for instance, in the army of the U.S. and in our army. The U.S. Army is capable of monitoring the situation from the ground --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe the question is: What's the means of your communication during that period? It's very simple. We don't have to involve Iraq here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, I just thought since we see all this modern equipment from North America, you know, that perhaps we could bring it into context in 1995 in Bosnia. Let me move on to the next question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We talked a little bit about the security organ, and then you were asked about some reports that were in a safe of the security organ. First of all, could you please tell us whether at the battalion level members of the security organ were required to report to the battalion commanders as to what they were reporting to the security organ higher up.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We discussed that in the private session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, we can go into the private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, there were a series of questions quoting from a UN report, and the suggestion might have been that perhaps you from your location were targeting the UN post over there. When you were in Banja Luka being questioned, the Prosecution at that time, I believe Mr. Butler was there, did they show you any photographs of your units attacking UN posts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he show you any photographs of the result of these attacks that they assert?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they show you any statements of witnesses who were there at the time under attack that would require them to notify the UN, so under the rules of engagement the UN can then bomb, as they did later on on the 11th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't show me that either, but if I may say one more thing on that issue. Had we done that, as it's claimed in the report, they had a possibility to report this to the organs in charge. And through our organs in charge, through the chief of staff or the duty operations officer, warn me to stop doing that. For a period of time, we had a telephone line, direct telephone line, with them that we used to communicate with. So I claim here that no one, either from the command to stop attacking them, and of course they didn't ask me to do that because I never attacked them. And in addition, they were not a problematic target. And it never occurred to me to attack them. I am a man who has high respect for UN institutions, and I myself applied to become a member of peacekeeping forces, so I would never have done such a thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you were asked some questions about some minutes working -- of a working meeting. I would like to go back on that and clarify one point. So I would like to show you what has been marked as D165/1. And we have some yellow stickies, both the one for the gentleman in his language and for us in English. And again, first of all, I'm going to read the section. I believe I have it underlined for you. This would be on 5 July 1995. And hopefully we will get an accurate translation as to what is on the paper itself. And then we can proceed from there. It says: "Chief of staff will go to the 1st Infantry Battalion to increase accuracy and direction of artillery fire." Now, could you please read out what it says in the handwritten version in the language in which it was written.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's an obvious mistake. I'm looking at this English translation. It says that: "The chief of staff should go to the 1st Battalion to direct the -- to precisely establish the fire and direction of firing weapons."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I want you to read it slowly without any comments so that we can -- okay. Just cekajte, wait a second. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The chief of staff should go to the 1st Infantry Battalion to establish precisely the fire and direction of firing weapons."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Concretely speaking, concretely, is artillery fire anywhere in the original version, not the one that was translated by whoever translated this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the original, it's not mentioned. Artillery fire is not mentioned in the original version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, in light of what you have in front of you, that is, the accurate version, could you please explain to us what exactly the chief of staff was supposed to do in accordance with this note that we have here.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The chief of staff was supposed only to help us in planning the fire, or rather, to see how we conceived the firing direction of certain weapons and range of fire so that we coordinate those and perhaps see whether any additional minefield should be laid up or any obstacles put up or to prepare better covers for -- and shelters for men. Also, to see how we had linked up with the adjacent battalions, whether there were any uncovered gaps, undefended gaps. Quite simply, to see the overall situation of our preparedness for carrying out defence operations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I believe we're through on that. I think we've clarified that issue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you were asked a series of questions about zone of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: That it is true that the word used in this item "orudje" is only used for artillery pieces and not for other weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In light of that --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Administratively, Your Honour, we have not objected to Mr. Karnavas trying to sort out translation errors on the cuff, because sometimes it can be helpful, but when you're talking about serious issues, we're inviting this kind of thing to happen. When there are translation issues, I think we need to invite the translation to go back for CLSS to deal with them, not suggesting that we put the people in the booth under the pressure to resolve these issues. Because this is now what we find ourselves in. It's more confusing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I just like to find out myself, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, yes, after this sitting, we'll entrust the registrar to ask the translation booth to check the exact translation of that phrase disparity. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just going back, just so there's no misunderstanding, was the chief of staff there to do anything --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I think this matter is over. I think you made your point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Please move on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were asked a series of questions about the term "zone of responsibility." Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This topic came up also when you were -- when you testified in the Krstic case, did it not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and this issue was raised while I gave statement to the Prosecution at their headquarters in Banja Luka. I also claimed at that time that a battalion doesn't have a zone of responsibility. But maybe due to some leading questions, I may have made a slip of the tongue and used the term "zone of responsibility."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So I take it you would not be surprised if we were to go through the transcript during the Krstic case where you emphatically note that you did not have a zone of responsibility --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa? No?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Obviously, an improper form of the question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I think we have already spent much more time on the zone of responsibility. The position of the Prosecution as well as the position of the witness is quite clear. I don't know which area are you going to clarify.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I just wanted to note for the record that under oath in a previous hearing, the gentleman emphatically stated the same as what he has under oath today, and that is when he was given the opportunity to question -- to answer a question regarding zones of responsibility, he indicated that neither the battalion nor brigade had a zone of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I don't see your point. I don't think it's useful to do this kind of practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's rehabilitation, Your Honour, just in case there was any, you know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We know the position. We know the answer of this witness. I think that's enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you indicate -- I just have one last question. You indicated that there was some -- you know, with respect to the attack on Srebrenica, you had indicated that you had expected an attack or had some information about a potential attack from the Muslim army that was in the demilitarised enclave, so-called demilitarised enclave during that period. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it you would not be surprised, then, to learn that just recently we received copies of intel reports, intelligence reports, related to Mr. Salapura that in the period of January to June 1995 that indicated that they had information that the 28th Division was about to attack? That would not surprise you, would it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wouldn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stojanovic, do you have any further cross?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, just two questions. Further cross-examination by Mr. Stojanovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Today, sir, you were asked about the 5th Engineering Battalion. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, first the company, then the battalion was mentioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. This is exactly where my questions are going in order to eliminate any possible dilemma. Is it true that as part of the Drina Corps there was the 5th Engineering Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose there was, but I don't know much about it. I know where they were located, but I don't know much about them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In any case, it was not part of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this unit headquartered in Konjevic Polje in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose there was -- it was, because there was some heavy machines there at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you perhaps know who was the commander of that unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that -- who the commander was later, because he was my senior at the academy. But before that -- I think it was Captain -- but I can't remember his last name. I think I saw him once. He was a tall man, and I think I saw him once in 1993 or 1994 when they were constructing a road. I can't remember his last name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me try to remind you. Was that the man whose last name was Avramovic [Realtime transcript read in error "Obramovic"]?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think that was his last name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am asking all these questions just for the record, that this unit is totally unrelated to Dragan Jokic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There could be no connection because it was subordinated to the corps. So there could be no connection and he could not have given them any orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. It has been brought to my attention that the last name in the transcript was not spelled correctly. It's Avramovic, with an A.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. At this stage, are there any documents to tender. Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. D185, to be under seal; then D183; D184; D186, that should be under seal; D187, that should be under seal as well; and then D188; and D189. And if you wish, I can give explanations as to each one of these.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any objections? Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, I'm just taking a look at the document. No, no objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Those documents are admitted into the evidence, with three of them under seal as indicated by the Defence counsel. And by the way, I think I have already informed the Defence team that as for the B/C/S version this Bench only needed two sets.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And how many is the Bench receiving, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, at least each of us will get a bundle of the documents, which is a heavy burden to us. And I guess it must be so with the Defence to copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I thought we rectified that situation, Your Honour, but I'll look into it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. At this stage are there any documents to tender on the Prosecution's side?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we will be tendering P863, that's the 4 June report or order, rather.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Is that all?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No objections, Your Honour, and we have no documents to be proposed to be tendered as exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just one other comment on the documents. Document P851, which is again the UN debriefing report. As you know, we have had an ongoing offering that into evidence; it's again referred to. I think I owe the Court a listing of all the times it was referred to by Mr. Butler and other witnesses and I'm still working on that. But I just would call your attention that we have an ongoing offer of that into evidence, just to remind everyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that. Well, this document P863/A is admitted into the evidence. It is so decided. Well, Witness, thank you very much for coming to The Hague to give your evidence. We wish you a pleasant journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, if there is nothing else, I would like to declare that the hearing for today is adjourned. And we will resume tomorrow morning at 9.00 in the same courtroom.
